Refused

$ pnx 18-extern-result.pnx
18-extern-result.pnx:1:8: extern: int, handle, str and cstr arguments (eight for C at most), one int or handle result; or fail only with a handle result
Diagnostics
ConditionMessage
A name that exists, without asthis name is already defined: give the function another with `as`
A signature not allowedextern: int, handle, str and cstr arguments (eight for C at most), one int or handle result; or fail only with a handle result
The host gives no such functionextern: the host does not give this function

19 The host interface§

(1) The host interface is one C header, pinax.h. It uses only <stddef.h> and <stdint.h> and reads as C99, C23 and C++. This clause defines what its functions do; the comments in the header give more detail for each.

(2) One state is used by one thread at a time; states share nothing. A pinax_str a function returns is valid until the next call on that state unless stated otherwise.

(3) PINAX_ABI names the binary interface: a host compiled against the header runs with any later library of the same PINAX_ABI. pinax_version() gives the library’s PINAX_VERSION_NUMBER(major, minor, patch) and pinax_abi() its PINAX_ABI; PINAX_ABI_OK() is true when the library has the header’s PINAX_ABI and at least its version, and a host checks it once, at start. Every error code and flag has its number written in the header and keeps it; a flag bit the library does not know is refused with PINAX_ERR_ARGUMENT. The fields named reserved_... must be 0 or NULL.

19.1 Error codes§

(1) Functions return a pinax_err; PINAX_OK is 0. Three outcomes are not failures: PINAX_SUSPENDED (the budget ran out, 19.5), PINAX_WAITING (every task waits for the host, 19.8) and PINAX_PENDING (a host procedure finishes later). From 0x100 come the faults and failures of scripts (the codes of 11.1); from 0x200 the failures of the interface itself: ARGUMENT, NO_ROOM (the block is too small), SYNTAX, TYPE (load refusals), NOT_FOUND, SIGNATURE, FORMAT, STATE (a call not allowed now).

(1a) From 0x400 come the failure codes a program declares (8.14), numbered in the order the state declares them. A procedure that fails with one gives that number; pinax_error_text gives its name. A host reads the name: the number of a code depends on what was loaded before it.

(2) pinax_error_text gives the last failure as text; for a fault, in the form module:line: name.

(3) A failure of the interface means the same in every function.

CodeMeaning
PINAX_ERR_ARGUMENTan argument is wrong: a null pointer, a procedure number that is none, a size other than the declaration’s
PINAX_ERR_NO_ROOMthe block has no room; pinax_needed says at least how big it had to be (19.3)
PINAX_ERR_SYNTAX PINAX_ERR_TYPEthe source was refused; the place and the reason are in diag and pinax_error_text
PINAX_ERR_NOT_FOUNDno procedure, global, module or host procedure of that name; also a host procedure not yet given again to a state opened from an image
PINAX_ERR_SIGNATUREthe signature differs: of the procedure looked for, of the host procedure registered, of the global shared
PINAX_ERR_FORMATa container, image or share file is not of this processor’s form, or failed its checks
PINAX_ERR_STATEa call not possible now: a run is suspended, a host procedure is running, no code is loaded, the state is frozen

19.2 Opening and closing§

(1) pinax_open(block, config, &state) opens a state inside block. Fields of config that are 0 take the processor’s defaults: the slots of the banks, the size of the main run’s region, the number of handles alive at once, the instruction budget of a run (0 for none), the function that receives load diagnostics. When the block is too small the answer is PINAX_ERR_NO_ROOM, and pinax_needed tells at least the size that would have been enough: the size up to what was being taken when the block ran out. A load may take more after that, so when the block opened again at that size runs out too, read it again.

(2) config.hash_key is the 16-byte key of the hash indexes use (8.10). A host that indexes text from outside gives a random key. All zeros means a fixed key.

(3) pinax_close closes the handles still open (calling their types’ close functions). It does not free the block; the block is the host’s.

(4) The block serves three uses. Opening takes the fixed parts of the state: the banks, the call frames, the main run’s region, the tables of host procedures and handles. With the defaults that is about 150 KB, most of it the region (64 KB) and the integer bank (32 KB), which config can shrink. The loaded program is stacked after it and stays. While a load runs, the unused tail of the block is the compiler’s working memory: about 20 KB for a small source, about 1 KB more per procedure, and 64 KB more when the source has a constant pattern (16.7). The working memory is free again when the load ends. A body uses working memory for the blocks it actually nests, not for the deepest nesting allowed.

19.3 Host procedures§

(1) pinax_register(state, module, defs, count) registers host functions as the procedures of one module. Each entry of defs has a name, a signature text (in the form of 9.2, such as "(s str gives n int or fail)"), the function, a user pointer and flags. Signatures are checked once, here. Register procedures before the sources that use them.

(2) A host function receives (call, user, args). Arguments and results are in arrays by type: integers (and bool, characters, handles and declared types over int) in args->i[] and args->ri[], strings in args->s[] and args->rs[], in the order of the signature, counted from 0 within each type. The integer pointers point straight at the state’s slots. A narrow integer of the signature (7.6) travels as one 64-bit slot, and after the function returns the processor checks the range of each result: outside it is the fault overflow (the result of a waiting procedure gets the same check in pinax_complete and ends with that code). An argument of pinax_run outside its narrow type is PINAX_ERR_ARGUMENT, and nothing runs. A float of the signature (7.7) travels in one integer slot too: the 64 bits of the slot are the bits of a double (moved with memcpy).

(3) When the function returns something other than PINAX_OK, a procedure whose signature has or fail fails with that code (11.2), and a procedure without it ends the run with a fault.

(4) A string result is copied into the caller’s region unless the procedure has the flag PINAX_WORD_KEEP_STR. With the flag it is not copied but pointed at; those bytes shall outlive the state and not change (static text, the program’s arguments and the like), and there is no limit to the number of such results. Room for new bytes comes from pinax_call_alloc, in the caller’s region. A parameter of type buffer in the signature is a buffer of the script: pinax_call_buffer gives its free room and is told how many bytes were filled.

19-host-words.c

#include "pinax.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

/* (s str gives r str): the result is written into the caller's region. */
static pinax_err shout(pinax_call *call, void *user, const pinax_args *args) {
    (void)user;
    pinax_mem room = pinax_call_alloc(call, args->s[0].len + 1);
    if (!room.ptr)
        return PINAX_ERR_FULL;                       /* no `or fail`: this is a fault */
    unsigned char *out = room.ptr;
    for (size_t k = 0; k < args->s[0].len; ++k) {
        unsigned char c = args->s[0].ptr[k];
        out[k] = c >= 'a' && c <= 'z' ? (unsigned char)(c - 32) : c;
    }
    out[args->s[0].len] = '!';
    args->rs[0] = (pinax_str){out, args->s[0].len + 1};
    return PINAX_OK;
}

/* (s str gives n int or fail): an outcome other than PINAX_OK is the word's failure. */
static pinax_err digits(pinax_call *call, void *user, const pinax_args *args) {
    (void)call; (void)user;
    int64_t n = 0;
    if (args->s[0].len == 0)
        return PINAX_ERR_FORMAT;
    for (size_t k = 0; k < args->s[0].len; ++k) {
        unsigned char c = args->s[0].ptr[k];
        if (c < '0' || c > '9')
            return PINAX_ERR_FORMAT;
        n = n * 10 + (c - '0');
    }
    args->ri[0] = n;
    return PINAX_OK;
}

/* (b buffer or fail): writes straight into a buffer the script declared. */
static pinax_err stamp(pinax_call *call, void *user, const pinax_args *args) {
    (void)user;
    pinax_mem room = pinax_call_buffer(call, args->i[0], 0);
    if (room.len < 5)
        return PINAX_ERR_FULL;
    memcpy(room.ptr, "[ok] ", 5);
    pinax_call_buffer(call, args->i[0], 5);
    return PINAX_OK;
}

int main(void) {
    static unsigned char block[1 << 20];
    pinax_config config = {.struct_size = sizeof config};
    pinax_state *st;
    if (pinax_open((pinax_mem){block, sizeof block}, &config, &st) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    static const pinax_word_def words[] = {
        {"shout", "(s str gives r str)", shout, NULL, 0},
        {"digits", "(s str gives n int or fail)", digits, NULL, 0},
        {"stamp", "(b buffer or fail)", stamp, NULL, 0},
    };
    pinax_register(st, "app", words, 3);
    static const char source[] =
        "use app .\n"
        "buffer line 32\n"
        "def demo gives s str do\n"
        "  line clear\n"
        "  line app.stamp or_else to e end\n"
        "  \"12x\" app.digits or_else to e -1 end to n\n"
        "  args \"hello\" app.shout \" \" \"42\" app.digits or_else to e -1 end \" \" n . cat line append or_else to e end\n"
        "  line contents\n"
        "end\n";
    if (pinax_load(st, "main", (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)source, sizeof source - 1}, PINAX_LOAD_CODE) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    pinax_word w;
    pinax_str out;
    if (pinax_find(st, "demo", "(gives s str)", 0, &w) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    pinax_run(st, w, &(pinax_args){.rs = &out});
    printf("%.*s\n", (int)out.len, (const char *)out.ptr);
    pinax_close(st);
    return 0;
}

Output

$ ./19-host-words
[ok] HELLO! 42 -1

19.4 Loading and lines§

(1) pinax_load(state, name, source, mode) loads a source (5.2). name is the module’s name; the modes are PINAX_LOAD_CODE and PINAX_LOAD_DATA (13.4). A refusal is PINAX_ERR_SYNTAX or PINAX_ERR_TYPE, and the diagnostic arrives at config.diag as (file, line, column, text).

(1a) pinax_load_bytecode(state, bytes) loads a bytecode container made by the processor into an empty state. The shape of a container is the processor’s (1 (3)). The processor does not trust a container; it checks it, and refuses with PINAX_ERR_FORMAT one that could break 4 (2a). Among what this implementation refuses: registers outside the window, jumps out of the procedure, a register read before it is written, a jump back or a call that does not charge the budget, a tail call to a procedure with other results, an operation that can fail without a failure procedure after it or with nothing after that, and an instruction that changes a string register and names it twice.

(1b) A load has no budget. So the processor loads a source or a container in time proportional to its length: no pass of it, finding names, deciding which procedures yield or checking the flow of the registers, grows with the square of the length. A host that takes untrusted sources therefore limits only their length, without fear that one load never ends.

(1c) A load into a state that already holds a program appends what the new source adds to the program and checks the new procedures only, so the bound of (1b) holds for the lines of a session and for modules loaded one by one. The declaration tables are kept the same way: a load reads what earlier loads declared where it lies and appends only its own declarations. The pass that decides which procedures yield covers the procedures the load brings, and the whole program only when the load redefines a procedure. The room the program takes in the block grows with what was declared: when a part has no room left to append to, the processor moves that part to a larger place, and when the load has ended it takes back the room it left; while a task (clause 14) is alive it does not, and the next load after the task has ended does. redefine appends the new body and leaves the old code where it was. The room used is read from block_bytes_used of pinax_stats. A session line that only runs code takes no room.

(1d) pinax_capacity(state, name, value) gives the number for a capacity written host (8 (4a)), before the load that has it. name is the declaration’s name: the plain name for the first source loaded, and module.name for any source. Giving a name again replaces its number. The state keeps up to 16 names of up to 47 bytes; a value is 1 to 231 − 1. A capacity may become a constant of the code (capacity, a check the loader proves against it), so exported code (19.11) made with one number may not be the code of a load with another; such a load runs without it.

19-capacity.c

#include "pinax.h"
#include <stdio.h>

/* The host knows at start how many requests it serves at once; the script leaves the number to it. */
int main(void) {
    static unsigned char block[1 << 20];
    pinax_config config = {.struct_size = sizeof config};
    pinax_state *st;
    if (pinax_open((pinax_mem){block, sizeof block}, &config, &st) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    static const char source[] =
        "tasks handlers host 32 8192 apart\n"
        "list seen int host\n"
        "def room gives n int do seen capacity end\n";
    const uint32_t at_once = 48;
    pinax_capacity(st, "handlers", at_once + 1); /* one more for the task that takes the requests */
    pinax_capacity(st, "seen", at_once);
    if (pinax_load(st, "main", (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)source, sizeof source - 1}, PINAX_LOAD_CODE) != PINAX_OK) {
        pinax_str why = pinax_error_text(st);
        fprintf(stderr, "%.*s\n", (int)why.len, (const char *)why.ptr);
        return 1;
    }
    pinax_word w;
    int64_t n = 0;
    pinax_find(st, "room", "(gives n int)", 0, &w);
    pinax_run(st, w, &(pinax_args){.ri = &n});
    printf("seen holds %lld\n", (long long)n);
    pinax_close(st);
    return 0;
}

Output

$ ./19-capacity
seen holds 48

(2) pinax_eval(state, text) runs one line as a session does. All lines form one module (the session). What a line leaves is read with pinax_eval_count and pinax_eval_value.

(2a) The session has a stack that stays from line to line. A line starts with what the lines before it left and is checked as a procedure whose inputs are those values and whose results are what it leaves. The session stack holds at most 16 values: an int or a type over it, a bool, an err, a str of at most 255 bytes, a handle that is not owned. A line that would leave more, or a collection, a rail or an owned value, is refused; one that leaves a longer str ends with PINAX_ERR_NO_ROOM after it ran. A line that is refused or ends with a fault leaves the stack as it was before it; so does one that ran out of budget and is abandoned, while one resumed to its end leaves what it left. A str of the session stack is copied into the state and stays valid until the next pinax_eval or pinax_eval_clear. pinax_eval_clear(state) empties the stack, as does a line that begins with the tool procedure clear. A load or a run leaves it as it is; an image and a clone do not carry it.

(3) pinax_on_barrier(state, function, user) gives the function a dot calls (10.8 (3)): at each dot the code reaches, and at the end of the code of a load or of a session line, also one that ends with a fault, the processor calls function(user). In it the host writes what its host procedures hold back and waits for what they started in the background; it does not call the state. NULL, the default, finishes nothing. A clone keeps the function; an image does not. The host library’s pinax_host_register_all gives one that writes the output io holds back.

(4) pinax_set_trace(state, function, user) asks for a trace of the lines of procedures. While a function is set, what the compiler produces from a load or a session line holds, at the start of each line of a procedure body (not of the top level), an instruction that calls function(user, line, word) as the line is about to run; pinax_fault_local then reads the locals the procedure holds there, as at a fault. The function may call only what reads the state. If it answers non-zero the run is suspended before that line (a breakpoint): the call that ran answers PINAX_SUSPENDED and pinax_resume goes on from the line, without calling the function for it again. Code compiled with no function set holds no such instruction and costs nothing; code that holds it runs on, calling nothing, once the function is NULL. An image and exported C do not carry the function or the instruction.

19.5 Finding and running§

(1) pinax_find(state, name, signature, flags, &word) finds a procedure and checks that its signature is the one given; another is PINAX_ERR_SIGNATURE. A bare name is a procedure of the first source loaded; module.procedure a procedure of that module (exported or not).

(2) pinax_run(state, word, args) runs a procedure. When the budget runs out it returns PINAX_SUSPENDED, and pinax_resume goes on where it stopped; the budget does not change results. A fault returns its code, and the state takes the next run. The budget bounds one slice, not the run: a script that never ends is suspended again and again, and the host decides how many slices it allows (or goes back to its event loop between two) and what it does when they are used up.

(2b) The three promises a host relies on can be checked on its own compiler and platform, with ./nob contract or by compiling this example: a block too small is refused with PINAX_ERR_NO_ROOM and pinax_needed names a size above it; a run resumed at its budget ends with the result of a run with no budget, and a script that never ends is stopped by the host; a registered C function is called with its arguments and its failure is the code of the run.

19-contract.c

#include "pinax.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

/* The three promises a host relies on, each checked in a few lines; run it on your own compiler and
   platform. It prints `ok` for each, or the check that failed, and exits with 0 only when all hold:
   1. the memory is the host's: a block that is too small is refused with PINAX_ERR_NO_ROOM (by the
      open or by the load), and pinax_needed names a size that is at least what was being taken;
   2. the run is the host's: the instruction budget bounds a slice, a run resumed to its end gives the
      result of a run with no budget at all, and a script that never ends is stopped by the host;
   3. the functions are the host's: a registered C function is called with its arguments, and its
      failure comes back as the code of the run. */

static int failed;
#define CHECK(what, ok) do { if (ok) printf("ok   %s\n", what); else { printf("FAIL %s\n", what); failed = 1; } } while (0)

static pinax_err tenfold(pinax_call *call, void *user, const pinax_args *args) {
    (void)call; (void)user;
    if (args->i[0] < 0)
        return PINAX_ERR_ARGUMENT;                  /* a failure of the host function: the code of the run */
    args->ri[0] = args->i[0] * 10;
    return PINAX_OK;
}

static int load(pinax_state *st, const char *text) {
    if (pinax_load(st, "main", (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)text, strlen(text)}, PINAX_LOAD_CODE) == PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    pinax_str why = pinax_error_text(st);
    printf("     refused: %.*s\n", (int)why.len, (const char *)why.ptr);
    return 0;
}

/* resumes a run for as long as the host allows; returns the last code and the slices it took */
static pinax_err slices(pinax_state *st, pinax_word w, pinax_args *args, int allowed, int *used) {
    pinax_err err = pinax_run(st, w, args);
    *used = 1;
    while (err == PINAX_SUSPENDED && *used < allowed) {
        err = pinax_resume(st, args);
        ++*used;
    }
    return err;
}

int main(void) {
    /* 1. a block too small: the open or the load answers PINAX_ERR_NO_ROOM, and pinax_needed says at least how much */
    static unsigned char block[1 << 20];
    pinax_config config = {.struct_size = sizeof config, .budget = 1000};
    pinax_state *st = NULL;
    pinax_err err;
    size_t small = 4096;
    while (small < sizeof block && (err = pinax_open((pinax_mem){block, small}, &config, &st)) != PINAX_OK)
        small *= 2;                                              /* the smallest block (a power of 2) a state opens in */
    static char big[40000];                                      /* a source of many procedures: more than the block has left */
    size_t n = 0;
    for (int k = 0; k < 400 && n + 80 < sizeof big; ++k)
        n += (size_t)snprintf(big + n, sizeof big - n, "def p%d n int gives r int do n %d add end\n", k, k);
    err = pinax_load(st, "main", (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)big, n}, PINAX_LOAD_CODE);
    CHECK("a load that does not fit is refused with PINAX_ERR_NO_ROOM", err == PINAX_ERR_NO_ROOM);
    const size_t needed = pinax_needed(st);
    CHECK("pinax_needed names a block size above the one that failed", needed > small);
    pinax_close(st);
    st = NULL;
    size_t again = needed;                                       /* pinax_needed is at least enough, and a load may take more: read it again */
    while (again <= sizeof block) {
        if (pinax_open((pinax_mem){block, again}, &config, &st) == PINAX_OK &&
            pinax_load(st, "main", (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)big, n}, PINAX_LOAD_CODE) == PINAX_OK)
            break;
        if (st)
            pinax_close(st);
        st = NULL;
        again = again * 3 / 2;
    }
    CHECK("opened again at that size (or a little more), the same source loads", st != NULL);
    if (st)
        pinax_close(st);
    st = NULL;
    CHECK("a block of 1 MB opens", pinax_open((pinax_mem){block, sizeof block}, &config, &st) == PINAX_OK);
    if (!st)
        return 1;

    /* 3. a registered C function */
    static const pinax_word_def words[] = {{"tenfold", "(n int gives r int or fail)", tenfold, NULL, 0}};
    CHECK("a C function is registered", pinax_register(st, "calc", words, 1) == PINAX_OK);
    CHECK("a script that uses it loads",
          load(st, "use calc .\n"
                   "def answer n int gives r int or fail do n calc.tenfold or_fail 2 add end\n"
                   "def tally n int gives r int do 0 to s  1 n 1 add range do to i s i add to s end each  s end\n"
                   "def spin do loop end end\n"));
    pinax_word answer, count, spin;
    pinax_find(st, "answer", "(n int gives r int or fail)", 0, &answer);
    int64_t in = 4, out = 0;
    pinax_args args = {.i = &in, .ri = &out};
    int used;
    err = slices(st, answer, &args, 100, &used);
    CHECK("the C function is called with its argument: answer(4) = 42", err == PINAX_OK && out == 42);
    in = -1;
    err = slices(st, answer, &args, 100, &used);
    CHECK("its failure is the code of the run (PINAX_ERR_ARGUMENT)", err == PINAX_ERR_ARGUMENT);

    /* 2. the budget bounds a slice, not the run */
    pinax_find(st, "tally", "(n int gives r int)", 0, &count);
    in = 100000;
    err = slices(st, count, &args, 100000, &used);
    const int64_t sliced = out;
    CHECK("a run of a hundred thousand turns is suspended at the budget (many slices)", err == PINAX_OK && used > 10);
    pinax_state *second;
    static unsigned char block2[1 << 20];
    pinax_config none = {.struct_size = sizeof none};                 /* budget 0: no limit */
    CHECK("a second state opens with no budget", pinax_open((pinax_mem){block2, sizeof block2}, &none, &second) == PINAX_OK);
    CHECK("the same script loads there", load(second, "def tally n int gives r int do 0 to s  1 n 1 add range do to i s i add to s end each  s end\n"));
    pinax_word count2;
    pinax_find(second, "tally", "(n int gives r int)", 0, &count2);
    int64_t out2 = 0;
    pinax_args args2 = {.i = &in, .ri = &out2};
    err = slices(second, count2, &args2, 1, &used);
    CHECK("the result of a resumed run equals the result of a run with no budget", err == PINAX_OK && used == 1 && out2 == sliced);
    pinax_close(second);

    pinax_find(st, "spin", "()", 0, &spin);
    pinax_args none_args = {0};
    err = slices(st, spin, &none_args, 50, &used);
    CHECK("a script that never ends is stopped by the host after 50 slices", err == PINAX_SUSPENDED && used == 50);

    pinax_close(st);
    puts(failed ? "contract: FAILED" : "contract: ok");
    return failed;
}

Output

$ ./19-contract
ok   a load that does not fit is refused with PINAX_ERR_NO_ROOM
ok   pinax_needed names a block size above the one that failed
ok   opened again at that size (or a little more), the same source loads
ok   a block of 1 MB opens
ok   a C function is registered
ok   a script that uses it loads
ok   the C function is called with its argument: answer(4) = 42
ok   its failure is the code of the run (PINAX_ERR_ARGUMENT)
ok   a run of a hundred thousand turns is suspended at the budget (many slices)
ok   a second state opens with no budget
ok   the same script loads there
ok   the result of a resumed run equals the result of a run with no budget
ok   a script that never ends is stopped by the host after 50 slices
contract: ok

(2a) The budget counts the cost of each check at a back branch or a call, the bytes the string procedures scan, and each turn that run_all gives a task (14.1 (2)), which costs one. So every run of a container the processor accepts meets the budget, even one whose tasks spawn and end without a loop of their own.

(3) While a run is stopped (PINAX_SUSPENDED, PINAX_WAITING), a new pinax_run is PINAX_ERR_STATE. The host either continues it to its end or gives it up with pinax_abort.

(3a) pinax_abort(state) ends a stopped run as a fault would: the handles the run opened are closed, its tasks are freed and its pending tokens are forgotten (pinax_complete with one of them is PINAX_ERR_NOT_FOUND). What it already stored in globals stays. When what stopped is the code of a load, the load is taken back as a failed one is. The state then takes the next run. With nothing stopped it is PINAX_ERR_STATE. A host that must take the globals back too saves an image (19.9) before the run.

19-run.c

#include "pinax.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

static void load(pinax_state *st, const char *text) {
    if (pinax_load(st, "main", (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)text, strlen(text)}, PINAX_LOAD_CODE) != PINAX_OK) {
        pinax_str why = pinax_error_text(st);
        printf("refused: %.*s\n", (int)why.len, (const char *)why.ptr);
    }
}

int main(void) {
    static unsigned char block[1 << 20];
    pinax_config config = {.struct_size = sizeof config, .budget = 1000};   /* instructions per run or resume */
    pinax_state *st;
    if (pinax_open((pinax_mem){block, sizeof block}, &config, &st) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    load(st,
         "def total n int gives r int do 0 to s  1 n 1 add range do to i s i add to s end each  s end\n"
         "def ratio a int, b int gives r int do a 100 mul b div end\n");

    pinax_word w;
    /* the signature asked for must be the word's */
    printf("find with another signature: %s\n",
           pinax_find(st, "total", "(gives r int)", 0, &w) == PINAX_ERR_SIGNATURE ? "PINAX_ERR_SIGNATURE" : "?");
    pinax_find(st, "total", "(n int gives r int)", 0, &w);
    int64_t n = 100000, r = 0;
    pinax_args args = {.i = &n, .ri = &r};
    int resumes = 0;
    pinax_err err = pinax_run(st, w, &args);
    while (err == PINAX_SUSPENDED && resumes < 100000) {   /* the budget ran out: go on where it stopped, as often as the host allows */
        ++resumes;
        err = pinax_resume(st, &args);
    }
    if (err != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;                                    /* not finished: no result to print */
    printf("total(100000) = %lld after %s resumes\n", (long long)r, resumes > 10 ? "many" : "few");

    /* a fault comes back as the error code, with its place in the error text */
    pinax_find(st, "ratio", "(a int, b int gives r int)", 0, &w);
    int64_t ab[2] = {3, 0};
    err = pinax_run(st, w, &(pinax_args){.i = ab, .ri = &r});
    pinax_str why = pinax_error_text(st);
    printf("ratio(3, 0): %s, \"%.*s\"\n", err == PINAX_ERR_DIV_ZERO ? "PINAX_ERR_DIV_ZERO" : "?", (int)why.len, (const char *)why.ptr);

    /* the state is still usable */
    ab[1] = 4;
    err = pinax_run(st, w, &(pinax_args){.i = ab, .ri = &r});
    printf("ratio(3, 4) = %lld\n", (long long)r);

    /* one line at a time, as a session does */
    const char *line = "6 7 mul \"done\"";
    if (pinax_eval(st, (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)line, strlen(line)}) == PINAX_OK) {
        for (uint32_t k = 0; k < pinax_eval_count(st); ++k) {
            pinax_value v;
            pinax_eval_value(st, k, &v);
            if (v.kind == PINAX_VALUE_INT)
                printf("value %u: %lld (%.*s)\n", k, (long long)v.i, (int)v.type.len, (const char *)v.type.ptr);
            else
                printf("value %u: %.*s (%.*s)\n", k, (int)v.s.len, (const char *)v.s.ptr, (int)v.type.len, (const char *)v.type.ptr);
        }
    }
    pinax_close(st);
    return 0;
}

Output

$ ./19-run
find with another signature: PINAX_ERR_SIGNATURE
total(100000) = 5000050000 after many resumes
ratio(3, 0): PINAX_ERR_DIV_ZERO, "main:2: div_zero"
ratio(3, 4) = 75
value 0: 42 (int)
value 1: done (str)

(4) pinax_run may be called from inside a host procedure too. There it runs only procedures found with the flag PINAX_FIND_NESTED, and procedures that may yield (14.2) cannot be found with that flag.

(5) pinax_word_effects(state, word, &effects) tells what a procedure may do beyond its stack and locals, worked out from the loaded code of the procedure and of every procedure it may call. effects.effects holds PINAX_EFFECT_READS_GLOBALS and PINAX_EFFECT_WRITES_GLOBALS (a list’s length, a queue and a task set count as globals), PINAX_EFFECT_READS_OUTSIDE and PINAX_EFFECT_WRITES_OUTSIDE (through host procedures), PINAX_EFFECT_YIELDS, PINAX_EFFECT_FAILS and PINAX_EFFECT_ANYTHING (a C function of extern); module and module_effects name the host modules it reaches (the first 16 of n_modules). A host procedure tells what it touches with the flags PINAX_WORD_READS and PINAX_WORD_WRITES of its registration; one with neither counts as both, and one with PINAX_WORD_PURE as neither. A call through a procedure value counts every procedure of the program with that signature, a spawned task every procedure without parameters and results. A host may refuse a program whose procedures reach what they should not.

19.6 Handles§

(1) pinax_handle_type makes a handle type with a name and a close function; scripts use the name as a type in signatures. pinax_handle_new makes a handle of a C pointer, pinax_handle_get gives a handle’s pointer (NULL for a handle given back), and pinax_handle_release gives a handle back.

(2) A handle is a number and a generation (as in 8.9). A script cannot get an address from a handle. The handles a run that ends with a fault opened are closed by the state, calling their close functions.

19-handles.c

#include "pinax.h"
#include <stdio.h>

typedef struct { int value; int open; } counter;
static counter pool_[4];
static uint32_t counter_type;

static void close_counter(void *object, void *user) {   /* called for handles the script never closed */
    (void)user;
    ((counter *)object)->open = 0;
    printf("closed by the state: counter at %d\n", ((counter *)object)->value);
}
static pinax_err c_new(pinax_call *call, void *user, const pinax_args *args) {
    (void)user;
    for (int k = 0; k < 4; ++k)
        if (!pool_[k].open) {
            pool_[k] = (counter){0, 1};
            pinax_handle h;
            pinax_err err = pinax_handle_new(pinax_call_state(call), counter_type, &pool_[k], &h);
            args->ri[0] = (int64_t)h;
            return err;
        }
    return PINAX_ERR_FULL;
}
static pinax_err c_bump(pinax_call *call, void *user, const pinax_args *args) {
    (void)user;
    counter *c = pinax_handle_get(pinax_call_state(call), counter_type, (pinax_handle)args->i[0]);
    if (!c)
        return PINAX_ERR_STALE;
    args->ri[0] = ++c->value;
    return PINAX_OK;
}
static pinax_err c_free(pinax_call *call, void *user, const pinax_args *args) {
    (void)user;
    counter *c = pinax_handle_get(pinax_call_state(call), counter_type, (pinax_handle)args->i[0]);
    if (c) {
        printf("freed by the script: counter at %d\n", c->value);
        c->open = 0;
    }
    return pinax_handle_release(pinax_call_state(call), counter_type, (pinax_handle)args->i[0]);
}

int main(void) {
    static unsigned char block[1 << 20];
    pinax_config config = {.struct_size = sizeof config};
    pinax_state *st;
    if (pinax_open((pinax_mem){block, sizeof block}, &config, &st) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    pinax_handle_type(st, "counter", close_counter, NULL, &counter_type);
    static const pinax_word_def words[] = {
        {"new", "(gives owned counter or fail)", c_new, NULL, 0},
        {"bump", "(c counter gives n int)", c_bump, NULL, 0},
        {"free", "(c owned counter)", c_free, NULL, 0},
    };
    pinax_register(st, "ctr", words, 3);
    static const char source[] =
        "use ctr .\n"
        "def twice gives n int or fail do\n"
        "  ctr.new or_fail to c\n"
        "  c ctr.bump drop  c ctr.bump to n\n"
        "  c ctr.free\n"
        "  n\n"
        "end\n"
        "def broken gives n int or fail do\n"
        "  ctr.new or_fail to c\n"
        "  c ctr.bump 0 div to n\n"            /* a fault while the counter is open */
        "  c ctr.free\n"
        "  n\n"
        "end\n";
    if (pinax_load(st, "main", (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)source, sizeof source - 1}, PINAX_LOAD_CODE) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    pinax_word w;
    int64_t n = 0;
    pinax_find(st, "twice", "(gives n int or fail)", 0, &w);
    pinax_run(st, w, &(pinax_args){.ri = &n});
    printf("twice = %lld\n", (long long)n);
    pinax_find(st, "broken", "(gives n int or fail)", 0, &w);
    pinax_err err = pinax_run(st, w, &(pinax_args){.ri = &n});
    printf("broken: %s\n", err == PINAX_ERR_DIV_ZERO ? "PINAX_ERR_DIV_ZERO" : "?");
    pinax_close(st);
    return 0;
}

Output

$ ./19-handles
freed by the script: counter at 2
twice = 2
closed by the state: counter at 1
broken: PINAX_ERR_DIV_ZERO

19.7 Binding§

(1) pinax_bind(state, global, memory, bytes) changes the storage of a global declared bound (8.12) to host memory; the size shall match the declaration: for an array, the cells times the bytes of a cell (the width of a narrow integer, 8 for any other value; 8.4). Script and host read and write the same bytes without copying. pinax_global_find tells where a declared global is and how large it is.

19-bind.c

#include "pinax.h"
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void) {
    static unsigned char block[1 << 20];
    pinax_config config = {.struct_size = sizeof config};
    pinax_state *st;
    if (pinax_open((pinax_mem){block, sizeof block}, &config, &st) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    static const char source[] =
        "bound array samples int 5\n"
        "bound global scale int\n"
        "def scaled_sum gives n int do samples sum scale mul end\n"
        "def clear_first do 0 0 set samples end\n";
    if (pinax_load(st, "main", (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)source, sizeof source - 1}, PINAX_LOAD_CODE) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    static int64_t samples[5] = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};    /* host memory the script reads and writes in place */
    static int64_t scale = 10;
    pinax_bind(st, "samples", samples, sizeof samples);
    pinax_bind(st, "scale", &scale, sizeof scale);
    pinax_word w;
    int64_t n = 0;
    pinax_find(st, "scaled_sum", "(gives n int)", 0, &w);
    pinax_run(st, w, &(pinax_args){.ri = &n});
    printf("scaled_sum = %lld\n", (long long)n);
    samples[4] = 105;                                /* the host changes it; no copy to refresh */
    pinax_run(st, w, &(pinax_args){.ri = &n});
    printf("after the host wrote samples[4]: %lld\n", (long long)n);
    pinax_find(st, "clear_first", "()", 0, &w);
    pinax_run(st, w, NULL);
    printf("after the script wrote cell 0: samples[0] = %lld\n", (long long)samples[0]);
    pinax_close(st);
    return 0;
}

Output

$ ./19-bind
scaled_sum = 150
after the host wrote samples[4]: 1150
after the script wrote cell 0: samples[0] = 0

(1a) pinax_share(state, global, source, from) gives a global that state declares shared (8.13) the storage of the global from of source, without copying. Kind, type and capacity must be the same, else PINAX_ERR_SIGNATURE. An index also needs the same hash key (19.2), and its table given first from the same source. A list keeps the length it has then. When a table is given again, its index is given again too.

(1b) A source that lent storage is frozen: pinax_run, pinax_load, pinax_eval and pinax_bind on it are PINAX_ERR_STATE from then on. So its bytes do not change, and states on several threads may read them at once. source must stay open while the states that borrow from it use it. Until every shared global is given, runs are refused with PINAX_ERR_NOT_FOUND. After an image is opened or a state cloned, give them again (19.9).

19-share.c

#include "pinax.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

/* One state holds the data; two others read it in place. Nothing is copied. */
static const char data[] =
    "record city\n  name str 12\n  people int\nend\n"
    "list cities city 8\n"
    "index by_name cities city.name\n"
    "row cities \"Seoul\" 9411 .\n"
    "row cities \"Busan\" 3317 .\n"
    "row cities \"Incheon\" 3001 .\n";
static const char reader[] =
    "record city\n  name str 12\n  people int\nend\n"
    "shared list cities city 8\n"
    "shared index by_name cities city.name\n"
    "def people_of name str gives n int or fail do name by_name lookup or_fail city.people end\n"
    "def total gives n int do\n"
    "  0 to t  0 to i\n"
    "  loop i cities len lt not if break . end  t i cities idx city.people add to t  i 1 add to i end\n"
    "  t\n"
    "end\n";

static pinax_state *open_in(unsigned char *block, size_t bytes) {
    pinax_config config = {.struct_size = sizeof config};
    pinax_state *st;
    return pinax_open((pinax_mem){block, bytes}, &config, &st) == PINAX_OK ? st : NULL;
}

static int64_t call(pinax_state *st, const char *word, const char *signature, const char *name, pinax_err *err) {
    pinax_word w;
    int64_t out = 0;
    pinax_str in = {(const unsigned char *)name, name ? strlen(name) : 0};
    pinax_args args = {.s = &in, .ri = &out};
    *err = pinax_find(st, word, signature, 0, &w);
    if (*err == PINAX_OK)
        *err = pinax_run(st, w, &args);
    return out;
}

int main(void) {
    static unsigned char blocks[3][1024 * 1024];
    pinax_state *source = open_in(blocks[0], sizeof blocks[0]);
    pinax_state *a = open_in(blocks[1], sizeof blocks[1]), *b = open_in(blocks[2], sizeof blocks[2]);
    if (!source || !a || !b || pinax_load(source, "data", (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)data, strlen(data)},
                                          PINAX_LOAD_DATA) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    pinax_err err;
    pinax_state *readers[2] = {a, b};
    for (int k = 0; k < 2; ++k) {
        if (pinax_load(readers[k], "main", (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)reader, strlen(reader)},
                       PINAX_LOAD_CODE) != PINAX_OK)
            return 1;
    }
    call(a, "total", "(gives n int)", NULL, &err);
    printf("before sharing: %#x (not found)\n", (unsigned)err);

    for (int k = 0; k < 2; ++k) /* the table first, then its index */
        if (pinax_share(readers[k], "cities", source, "cities") != PINAX_OK ||
            pinax_share(readers[k], "by_name", source, "by_name") != PINAX_OK)
            return 1;
    printf("a: Busan has %lld\n", (long long)call(a, "people_of", "(name str gives n int or fail)", "Busan", &err));
    printf("b: total %lld\n", (long long)call(b, "total", "(gives n int)", NULL, &err));

    pinax_global mine, theirs;
    pinax_global_find(source, "cities", &theirs);
    pinax_global_find(b, "cities", &mine);
    printf("same bytes: %s\n", mine.ptr == theirs.ptr ? "yes" : "no");
    err = pinax_load(source, "more", (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)"global x int\n", 13}, PINAX_LOAD_CODE);
    printf("the source loads again: %#x (state)\n", (unsigned)err);
    pinax_close(a);
    pinax_close(b);
    pinax_close(source);
    return 0;
}

Output

$ ./19-share
before sharing: 0x204 (not found)
a: Busan has 3317
b: total 15729
same bytes: yes
the source loads again: 0x207 (state)

(1c) Several processes share through a file. pinax_share_save(source, out, &written) writes the globals of source that can be shared (scalars, arrays, lists, buffers and indexes; not those it declares shared itself) into one file without addresses; pinax_share_size is its length. Saving copies, so source is not frozen. The host library’s pinax_map_file(path, &bytes, &map) maps the file read-only, so that the processes that map the same file use the same pages. pinax_share_file(state, global, bytes, from) gives the file’s global from, with the checks of (1a); an index needs the hash key of the file and its table given first from the same file. The file’s head, the size and length of each global and the slots of an index are checked, else PINAX_ERR_FORMAT; its other bytes are trusted as an image’s are (19.9), except that no more than N bytes are read from a str N cell whose length byte says more. bytes starts on a 16-byte boundary and outlives the states that read it: call pinax_unmap_file after they are closed.

19-share-file.c

#include "pinax.h"
#include "pinax_host.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

/* One program writes the data as a share file; any number of processes map it and read it in
   place. Here the same program maps it twice, as two processes would. */
static const char data[] =
    "record city\n  name str 12\n  people int\nend\n"
    "list cities city 8\n"
    "index by_name cities city.name\n"
    "row cities \"Seoul\" 9411 .\n"
    "row cities \"Busan\" 3317 .\n";
static const char reader[] =
    "record city\n  name str 12\n  people int\nend\n"
    "shared list cities city 8\n"
    "shared index by_name cities city.name\n"
    "def people_of name str gives n int or fail do name by_name lookup or_fail city.people end\n";

static unsigned char blocks[3][1024 * 1024];

static int write_file(const char *path) {
    pinax_config config = {.struct_size = sizeof config};
    pinax_state *source;
    if (pinax_open((pinax_mem){blocks[0], sizeof blocks[0]}, &config, &source) != PINAX_OK ||
        pinax_load(source, "data", (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)data, strlen(data)}, PINAX_LOAD_DATA) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    size_t size = pinax_share_size(source), written = 0;
    unsigned char *bytes = malloc(size);
    if (!bytes || pinax_share_save(source, (pinax_mem){bytes, size}, &written) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "wb");
    int bad = !f || fwrite(bytes, 1, written, f) != written;
    bad |= f && fclose(f) != 0;
    printf("wrote %zu bytes\n", written);
    free(bytes);
    pinax_close(source); /* the file needs nothing of it */
    return bad;
}

static void read_file(const char *path, unsigned char *block, size_t bytes, const char *name) {
    pinax_config config = {.struct_size = sizeof config};
    pinax_state *st;
    pinax_str file;
    pinax_mapping *map;
    pinax_word w;
    int64_t out = 0;
    pinax_str in = {(const unsigned char *)name, strlen(name)};
    pinax_args args = {.s = &in, .ri = &out};
    if (pinax_map_file(path, &file, &map) != PINAX_OK)
        return;
    if (pinax_open((pinax_mem){block, bytes}, &config, &st) == PINAX_OK &&
        pinax_load(st, "main", (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)reader, strlen(reader)}, PINAX_LOAD_CODE) == PINAX_OK &&
        pinax_share_file(st, "cities", file, "cities") == PINAX_OK &&      /* the table first */
        pinax_share_file(st, "by_name", file, "by_name") == PINAX_OK &&    /* then its index */
        pinax_find(st, "people_of", "(name str gives n int or fail)", 0, &w) == PINAX_OK &&
        pinax_run(st, w, &args) == PINAX_OK)
        printf("%s has %lld\n", name, (long long)out);
    pinax_close(st);
    pinax_unmap_file(map); /* after the state that read it */
}

int main(void) {
    const char *path = "cities.pnxs";
    if (write_file(path) != 0)
        return 1;
    read_file(path, blocks[1], sizeof blocks[1], "Seoul");
    read_file(path, blocks[2], sizeof blocks[2], "Busan");
    remove(path);
    return 0;
}

Output

$ ./19-share-file
wrote 528 bytes
Seoul has 9411
Busan has 3317

(1d) While a run is not finished — suspended by the budget, waiting for a host operation, or inside a host procedure — pinax_bind, pinax_share and pinax_share_file are PINAX_ERR_STATE: a view the run holds may point into the storage they would replace.

(2) The number that pinax_global_find gives is what a procedure with a collection parameter (9.9) takes as that argument, an integer in i. A number of a collection of another kind or another size of element, or of no global, is the fault PINAX_ERR_STATE where the procedure uses it.

19.8 Host procedures that finish later§

(1) A host procedure registered with PINAX_WORD_AWAITABLE may start some work, take a token with pinax_call_pending, and return PINAX_PENDING. The task that called it waits and others run. When nothing else can run, pinax_run or pinax_resume returns PINAX_WAITING. The host finishes the work with pinax_complete(state,
token, outcome, values) and calls pinax_resume.

19-await.c

#include "pinax.h"
#include <stdio.h>

/* A host word that finishes later: it starts the work, keeps a token and returns PINAX_PENDING. */
static pinax_token waiting[4];
static int64_t asked[4];
static int n_waiting;
static pinax_err fetch(pinax_call *call, void *user, const pinax_args *args) {
    (void)user;
    asked[n_waiting] = args->i[0];
    waiting[n_waiting++] = pinax_call_pending(call);
    return PINAX_PENDING;
}

int main(void) {
    static unsigned char block[1 << 20];
    pinax_config config = {.struct_size = sizeof config};
    pinax_state *st;
    if (pinax_open((pinax_mem){block, sizeof block}, &config, &st) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    static const pinax_word_def words[] = {{"fetch", "(n int gives r int or fail)", fetch, NULL, PINAX_WORD_AWAITABLE}};
    pinax_register(st, "net", words, 1);
    static const char source[] =
        "use net .\n"
        "tasks workers 2\n"
        "list got int 4\n"
        "def both gives r int do\n"
        "  do 1 net.fetch or_else to e -1 end got push or_else to e end end workers spawn or_else to e 0 return end drop\n"
        "  do 2 net.fetch or_else to e -1 end got push or_else to e end end workers spawn or_else to e 0 return end drop\n"
        "  workers run_all\n"
        "  got sum\n"
        "end\n";
    if (pinax_load(st, "main", (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)source, sizeof source - 1}, PINAX_LOAD_CODE) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    pinax_word w;
    int64_t r = 0;
    pinax_args args = {.ri = &r};
    pinax_find(st, "both", "(gives r int)", 0, &w);
    pinax_err err = pinax_run(st, w, &args);
    printf("run: %s, %d operations started\n", err == PINAX_WAITING ? "PINAX_WAITING" : "?", n_waiting);
    /* the host finishes them in its own time, here the second first */
    for (int k = n_waiting - 1; k >= 0; --k) {
        int64_t result = asked[k] * 100;
        pinax_complete(st, waiting[k], PINAX_OK, &(pinax_args){.ri = &result});
    }
    err = pinax_resume(st, &args);
    printf("resume: %s, both = %lld\n", err == PINAX_OK ? "PINAX_OK" : "?", (long long)r);
    pinax_close(st);
    return 0;
}

Output

$ ./19-await
run: PINAX_WAITING, 2 operations started
resume: PINAX_OK, both = 300

(2) In a state the host loop (17.4) runs, a host procedure takes its token with pinax_loop_pending in place of pinax_call_pending and finishes the work with pinax_loop_complete, from any thread. The loop calls pinax_complete on the state’s thread and continues the run.

19.9 Images and clones§

(1) An image is a whole state: code, declarations, globals, slots, regions, stopped runs and tasks. pinax_image_save writes it and pinax_image_open opens it. An image that lies at the start of the block is opened in place, without copying. An image of another format, or of another build’s memory layout, is PINAX_ERR_FORMAT.

(1a) An image is data the host vouches for (4 (2a)): the processor checks its head, format and layout, and that the addresses inside it lie in the block it was saved from, but not every byte. Open only images this host or one it trusts saved. Strings that pointed outside the block (a host’s text) and the last pattern match do not survive an image.

(2) On an opened state the host gives host procedures, handle types and extern functions again, by name. Until all are given, runs are refused with PINAX_ERR_NOT_FOUND. Handles come back closed (without their close functions), and bound globals back on their own storage. pinax_clone saves and opens in another block in one call.

(2a) A clone opens in a block of pinax_image_size(source) bytes or more; a smaller block is PINAX_ERR_NO_ROOM.

(2b) pinax_clone_with(source, block, flags, out) is pinax_clone with flags. With PINAX_CLONE_KEEP_HOSTS the clone keeps what the source was given in this process, with the same user pointers: its host procedures, handle types, extern functions and resolver, its exported code (19.11) and its task fault function (19.10 (3a)). So it runs at once. Bound globals are bound again and handles do not pass, as for any clone. An unknown flag is PINAX_ERR_ARGUMENT.

19-image.c

#include "pinax.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

static pinax_err twice(pinax_call *call, void *user, const pinax_args *args) {
    (void)call; (void)user;
    if (args->i[0] > INT64_MAX / 2 || args->i[0] < INT64_MIN / 2)
        return PINAX_ERR_OVERFLOW;
    args->ri[0] = args->i[0] * 2;
    return PINAX_OK;
}
static const pinax_word_def words[] = {{"twice", "(n int gives r int)", twice, NULL, 0}};

static int64_t call_next(pinax_state *st) {
    pinax_word w;
    int64_t r = 0;
    if (pinax_find(st, "next", "(gives r int)", 0, &w) != PINAX_OK)
        return -1;
    pinax_err err = pinax_run(st, w, &(pinax_args){.ri = &r});
    return err == PINAX_OK ? r : -(int64_t)err;
}

int main(void) {
    static _Alignas(16) unsigned char a[1 << 20], b[1 << 20], c[1 << 20];
    pinax_config config = {.struct_size = sizeof config};
    pinax_state *st;
    if (pinax_open((pinax_mem){a, sizeof a}, &config, &st) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    pinax_register(st, "host", words, 1);
    static const char source[] =
        "use host .\n"
        "global calls int\n"
        "def next gives r int do calls 1 add set calls  calls host.twice end\n";
    if (pinax_load(st, "main", (pinax_str){(const unsigned char *)source, sizeof source - 1}, PINAX_LOAD_CODE) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    call_next(st);
    printf("in the first state: %lld\n", (long long)call_next(st));

    /* save the whole state: code, globals, everything */
    size_t size = pinax_image_size(st), written = 0;
    unsigned char *image = malloc(size);
    pinax_image_save(st, (pinax_mem){image, size}, &written);

    /* open it in another block; host words are given again by name */
    pinax_state *copy;
    if (pinax_image_open((pinax_mem){b, sizeof b}, (pinax_str){image, written}, &config, &copy) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    printf("before the host word is given again: %s\n", call_next(copy) == -PINAX_ERR_NOT_FOUND ? "PINAX_ERR_NOT_FOUND" : "?");
    pinax_register(copy, "host", words, 1);
    printf("the copy goes on: %lld\n", (long long)call_next(copy));
    printf("the first state is its own: %lld\n", (long long)call_next(st));

    /* a clone is the same in one call */
    pinax_state *twin;
    if (pinax_clone(copy, (pinax_mem){c, sizeof c}, &twin) != PINAX_OK)
        return 1;
    pinax_register(twin, "host", words, 1);
    printf("the clone of the copy: %lld\n", (long long)call_next(twin));
    free(image);
    pinax_close(twin);
    pinax_close(copy);
    pinax_close(st);
    return 0;
}

Output

$ ./19-image
in the first state: 4
before the host word is given again: PINAX_ERR_NOT_FOUND
the copy goes on: 6
the first state is its own: 6
the clone of the copy: 8

19.10 Measuring, and the locals of a fault§

(1) pinax_stats_get gives the highest use of slots, region, handles and call depth, and the number of instructions run. It is for choosing the block and the capacities.

(2) pinax_fault_local gives, after a run that ended with a fault, the locals of the procedure the fault happened in with their values at that time (up to 16; text cut to its first 32 bytes, and shown only when its bytes lie in memory the state can vouch for). They are what pnx shows below a fault (11.3).

(3) pinax_task_faults gives how many tasks of apart groups (14.4 (3a)) ended with a fault since the state opened, and where the last one happened and why, in the form of a fault’s place (module:line: error). After the run that had it, pinax_fault_local reads that task’s locals, until the next run ends.

(3a) pinax_on_task_fault(state, fn, user) has the state call fn(user, state, fault) once for each such fault, at the fault, before the task’s slot is used again. fault gives the fault, the task’s tag (14.5) and its place in the same form. Several tasks that fault in one run are told one by one. Inside fn, pinax_fault_local reads the locals of that task. The run is in the middle, so fn may call only the functions that read the state: pinax_fault_local, pinax_task_faults, pinax_error_text. NULL takes the function away. An image and a clone forget it, as they forget host procedures (19.9), unless the clone keeps them (19.9 (2b)).

19.11 Exported code§

(1) pnx export-c (20 (3)) writes a program’s code as C. The host compiles that file with pinax_native.h of the same build and gets one pinax_native table. It covers the program as it was exported: its code and its procedures, counted in code_words and words. pinax_native_attach(state, table) makes the state run that code through the table from the first run at which the state’s program begins with the one exported: the same code, the same start of every procedure, the same build. Given before the loads, it serves a load’s own code too. NULL takes it back.

(1a) What is loaded after it (the lines of a session, a module loaded later) is interpreted, and the table stays in use: a call, a return or a task switch that goes into the code it covers runs there through the table again. A redefinition (20.4 (2a)) of one of its procedures with the same signature changes the program it covers: from then on the table is not used. One with another signature leaves the code it covers as it was, and the table stays in use.

(2) A program and a host see the same as interpreted: results, faults with their places and locals, failures, the budget (a run stops at the same CHECKs), waiting and tasks. Exported code does not make the checks the loader proved cannot fire (20 (1b)); a build with PINAX_CHECK_PROOFS makes them and stops the program when one fires.

(3) An image does not carry the table: attach it again. Nor does a clone, unless it is made with PINAX_CLONE_KEEP_HOSTS (19.9 (2b)). Attaching while a run is suspended or waits is PINAX_ERR_STATE. A table whose struct_size is another, or with one of code_words and words 0 and the other not, is PINAX_ERR_ARGUMENT; both 0 is a table of the whole program, whatever its length.

(4) The table is data the host vouches for, as an image is (4 (2a)): only its hash is checked, not its machine code. For exported code the guarantee of 4 (2a) holds as far as the loader’s proofs are right.

19.12 Callbacks§

(1) The library calls the host back in seven places: a host procedure, the barrier function, the trace function, the task fault function, config.diag, a handle type’s close function and the extern resolver (18). Each runs on the thread that is using the state (under pinax_loop, a loop thread). While one runs, the state knows which, and a call into the state that the table does not allow is refused: a function that returns pinax_err answers PINAX_ERR_STATE, one that returns a size, a count or a pointer answers 0 or NULL, one that returns nothing does nothing; the error text names the callback. Callbacks nest: a word run from a host procedure calls host procedures of its own, and each is a host procedure while it runs.

InsideThe state may be called with
a host procedurepinax_call_...; pinax_find with PINAX_FIND_NESTED, pinax_global_find; pinax_run of a word so found; pinax_handle_new, pinax_handle_get, pinax_handle_release; the functions that read
barrier, trace, task fault, diagthe functions that read
a handle type’s closepinax_handle_get and pinax_handle_release (an object that closes the objects it owns)
the resolvernothing

(2) The functions that read are pinax_error_text, pinax_needed, pinax_fault_local, pinax_task_faults, pinax_eval_count, pinax_eval_value, pinax_word_at, pinax_image_size, pinax_share_size and pinax_stats_get. pinax_close is never called from a callback.

(3) What a callback is given lives for that call only: the string arguments of a host procedure (views, not copies), the str and cstr arguments of a C function of extern (it neither keeps nor writes through them), the pinax_call of a host procedure, the task fault’s where, the trace’s procedure name and the diag message. pinax_call_alloc memory lives until the next run started by the host. pinax_loop_done is not a callback of the state: the run has ended when it is called, and it may start another.

(4) The host library is not free of process-wide data, as the core is: standard input read ahead, the random generator, the arguments of env, and the flush of standard output by its barrier are shared by every state of the process; pinax_host_exit_asked answers for the calling thread.

20 The command pnx§

(1) pnx is a host that uses this library, and a development tool. It registers all the standard host modules (clause 17).

pnx [--stats] [--lib NAME=PATH]... [--capacity NAME=N]... file.pnx [arguments]
pnx test file.pnx
pnx repl
pnx see file.pnx
pnx see --code file.pnx
pnx fmt file.pnx
pnx export-c file.pnx [NAME]

20.1 Running§

(1) pnx file.pnx arguments… loads the file and runs its load code. For each module the file uses or names in set_order that is not registered, it first loads MODULE.pnx from beside the file (13.1, 13.5). The file is loaded as the module named after it without .pnx; when that name is not written like a procedure (it begins with a digit or contains -), the module has no name.

(2) There are three exit statuses, and the one a program gives with sh.exit (17.5).

StatusWhen
0the load code ran to its end; for pnx test, every test passed
1a refusal: file:line:column: reason on standard error; a fault: file:line: kind and the locals of the procedure; for pnx test, a test failed
2the command line is wrong (the usage is shown), the file cannot be read, a library of --lib cannot be opened, a --capacity is not NAME=N

(3) --lib NAME=PATH opens the shared library at PATH so that the resolver finds its functions for extern … from "NAME" (clause 18). It finds only the functions that library defines (not those it imports). Without --lib, every extern is refused.

(3c) pnx see --code file.pnx loads the file without running it and lists the instructions of its procedures, one to a line: the address in the procedure, the name of the instruction and its fields, and the second word of an instruction that has one. It is for reading the code the compiler makes (how many instructions a turn of a loop costs); the format is not stable.

(3b) --stats writes one line to standard error after the run, the highest use of a state as pinax_stats_get gives it (19.10): pnx: stats: N instructions; highest use: int slots A, str slots B, region R bytes, handles H, call depth D; block U of B bytes (P percent). Standard output and the exit status are unchanged. It is how to read what a script needs from a real input.

(3a) --capacity NAME=N gives the capacity a source writes host (8 (4a), 19.4 (1d)), for a run, pnx test, pnx see, pnx export-c and pnx repl. A plain NAME is a declaration of the file, MODULE.NAME one of a module it uses. N is 1 to 231 − 1, and at most 16 are given. Without it, a source that writes host is refused at load, with the name of the capacity.

(3d) What the script writes with io.print and io.println is kept in a buffer and written when the buffer is full, before io.eprint and clock.sleep, before io.read_line asks the system for more of standard input, and when the run ends or faults. So standard output and standard error come out in the order the script wrote them, and a prompt shows before the program waits for a line. Except in pnx repl, io.read_line reads standard input ahead; a line already read ahead is given without writing. A host that embeds the library writes and reads both without a buffer.

20.2 Tests§

Syntax
test = "test" NAME "do" { body } "end" ;

(1) test NAME do … end defines a test: a procedure that takes and gives nothing. Tests do not run at load. pnx test file.pnx runs the tests of the file in order, writes ok or FAIL for each, and exits with 0 when all pass, 1 otherwise. A fault inside a test (a false assert included) is that test’s failure.

20-test.pnx

use str .
def middle s str gives str do s 1 str.skip 1 str.skip_last end
test middle_trims_both_ends do
  "[abc]" middle "abc" eq assert
end
test middle_of_two_is_empty do
  "ab" middle str.is_empty assert
end

Test run

$ pnx test 20-test.pnx
ok   middle_trims_both_ends
ok   middle_of_two_is_empty
2 tests, 0 failed

20-test-fail.pnx

def twice n int gives int do n 2 mul end
test doubles do 21 twice 42 eq assert end
test wrong do 21 twice 43 eq assert end

test-fail

$ pnx test 20-test-fail.pnx
ok   doubles
FAIL wrong (failed)
2 tests, 1 failed

20.3 Sessions§

(1) pnx repl reads lines from standard input and runs them one at a time (pinax_eval of 19.4). After each line it writes the session stack on standard output, the deepest value first, when it is not empty. A line can use what earlier lines defined and the values they left (19.4 (2a)). A line that ends inside a definition or a block is read together with the next. A line that is refused or ends with a fault leaves the stack as it was. The end of a line, Enter, is a dot (10.8): what the line wrote is on the screen before the prompt comes back.

(2) There are tool procedures only for sessions: list_words (the procedures defined), stack (the types on the stack there), clear (at the start of a line: the line starts from an empty stack), see (the stack after every line of the definitions that follow), redefine def … (the same as def … for a procedure that exists, (2a)). get_order (13.5 (3a)) tells the search order, in a session and in a file.

(2a) def NAME … with the name of a procedure an earlier line of the session defined redefines it. With the same signature, every procedure that calls it calls the new one. With another signature the new procedure takes the name; the procedures compiled before keep calling the old body, which no longer has a name, and pnx repl names them (“2 procedures still call the old sq: quad, cube”). One procedure is redefined in a line, and none while a task is alive. A procedure of a module loaded from a file is not redefined in the session: edit the file and load it again.

20-repl.pnx

use str .
3 4
mul
def sq n int gives int do n n mul end
sq
"x" 3 str.repeat
1 0 div
clear
2 sq

Session

$ pnx repl
3 4
12
12
144
144 "xxx"
error: line 1: div_zero
4

20.4 Showing the stack, and formatting§

(1) pnx see file.pnx shows, for every line of a definition, the stack (as types) where that line ends.

20-see.pnx

use str .
def tally s str gives n int, longest int do
  0 to n
  0 to longest
  s str.words do to w
    n 1 add to n
    w str.len
    longest max to longest
  end each
  n longest
end

Listing

$ pnx see 20-see.pnx
    3    0 to n                                         | (empty)
    4    0 to longest                                   | (empty)
    5    s str.words do to w                            | (empty)
    6      n 1 add to n                                 | (empty)
    7      w str.len                                    | int
    8      longest max to longest                       | (empty)
    9    end each                                       | (empty)
   10    n longest                                      | int int

(1a) When the source is refused, pnx see shows the lines before the place of the refusal, gives the diagnostic, and exits with 1.

20-see-refused.pnx

def f n int gives int do
  n 1 add
  n
end

Listing, then the refusal

$ pnx see 20-see-refused.pnx
    2    n 1 add                                        | int
    3    n                                              | int int
20-see-refused.pnx:4:1: the stack does not hold exactly the results of the signature here

(1b) pnx see --checks file.pnx loads the file as pnx file.pnx does (the code outside definitions runs), then shows, per procedure, the run-time checks the loader proved cannot fire: the procedure’s number of checks and of proven ones, and for each proven instruction its line, the instruction and the reason. A proof changes nothing a program does; the checks still run.

20-see-checks.pnx

use io .
use str .
const days 7
array rain int days
record city
  name str 8
  people int
end
list cities city 4
def wettest gives int do                      rem the index of the largest cell
  0 to best
  0 rain len range do to i
    i rain idx  best rain idx  gt if i to best end
  end each
  best
end
def people_of i int gives int do i cities idx city.people end
assign rain (3, 0, 12, 7, 0, 1, 2)
wettest str.to_str io.println

Output, then the checks

$ pnx see --checks 20-see-checks.pnx
2
word wettest: 3 checks, 3 proven
  line 13: AGET: the index lies below the capacity of the array
  line 13: AGET: the index lies below the capacity of the array
  line 14: ADDI: the operands are in ranges whose result fits
word people_of: 2 checks, 1 proven
  line 17: FGET: the row passed this table's check before
word (load): 7 checks, 7 proven
  line 18: ASET: the index lies below the capacity of the array
  line 18: ASET: the index lies below the capacity of the array
  line 18: ASET: the index lies below the capacity of the array
  line 18: ASET: the index lies below the capacity of the array
  line 18: ASET: the index lies below the capacity of the array
  line 18: ASET: the index lies below the capacity of the array
  line 18: ASET: the index lies below the capacity of the array

(1c) pnx see --effects file.pnx loads the file without running it and shows, for each procedure of the file, what it may do beyond its stack and locals (pinax_word_effects, 19.5 (5)): the globals it reads and writes, the host modules it reaches and whether it reads or writes through them, “anything (a C function)” for extern, “may yield” and “may fail”; “none” for a procedure that uses only its stack and locals.

20-see-effects.pnx

use io .
global total int
def sq n int gives int do n n mul end
def add_up n int do total n add set total end
def report do args "total " total sq . cat io.println end
def ask gives line str or fail do io.read_line or_fail end

The effects of each procedure

$ pnx see --effects 20-see-effects.pnx
sq: none
add_up: reads total; writes total
report: reads total; io writes
ask: io reads; may fail

(2) pnx fmt file.pnx writes the text with only indentation and spaces changed to standard output. Tokens, line breaks and remarks stay where they are. Formatting the result again changes nothing.

20-fmt.pnx

use io .
def sign n int gives r int do
n 0 gt if
1
   else   
n 0 lt if -1 else 0 end
end
end

Formatted

$ pnx fmt 20-fmt.pnx
use io .
def sign n int gives r int do
  n 0 gt if
    1
  else
    n 0 lt if -1 else 0 end
  end
end

(3) pnx export-c file.pnx [NAME] loads the file as pnx file.pnx does but runs none of its code, and writes the program’s code as C to standard output: a file that defines the table NAME (pnx_native when left out) for pinax_native_attach (19.11). Tool output, such as that of get_order, goes to standard error.

Annex A The whole grammar (normative)§

(1) This annex collects the syntax rules of the clauses in one place. The notation is that of ISO/IEC 14977: a b is sequence, a | b choice, [ a ] optional, { a } zero or more times, (* … *) a remark, ? … ? a rule stated in words. Names in capitals are the tokens of clause 6. Any number of spaces and remarks may stand between tokens, except right before a new name (6.3 (4)).

(2) The grammar is read with one token of lookahead. The exception is a parameter of a signature, where the token after it tells whether it is a name or a type. What a name refers to (a local, a global, a procedure) and the types on the stack are settled by the declarations and checks, not by the grammar.

(* 6: tokens *)
NAME        = letter { letter | digit } ;                (* not a reserved word *)
PATH        = NAME "." member { "." member } ;           (* member: a run of letters and digits *)
INT         = [ "+" | "-" ] ( digits | "0x" hex-digits | "0b" bit-digits ) ;
DEC         = [ "+" | "-" ] digits "." digits ;              (* 7.5 *)
FLOAT       = [ "+" | "-" ] digits [ "." digits ] "e" [ "+" | "-" ] digits
            | [ "+" | "-" ] "0x" hex-digits [ "." hex-digits ] "p" [ "+" | "-" ] digits ;   (* 7.7 *)
CHAR        = [ "U" ] "'" ( char-byte | escape ) "'" ;
STRING      = '"' { string-byte | escape } '"' ;
RAWSTRING   = "r" '"' { raw-byte } '"' ;
TEXT        = "text" TAG newline { text-line newline } TAG ;
BOOL        = "true" | "false" ;
literal     = INT | DEC | FLOAT | CHAR | STRING | RAWSTRING | TEXT | BOOL ;

(* 6.7, 13: a source *)
source      = [ "pinax" INT ] { item } ;
item        = import | order | forward | declaration | definition | row-item | assign-item | body ;
import      = "use" NAME [ "as" NAME ] "." ;
order       = "set_order" { order-one } "." | "get_order" ;   (* 13.5 *)
order-one   = NAME | "get_order" ;
forward     = "forward" ( "array" | "list" | "pool" ) NAME
            | "forward" NAME effect "end" ;

(* 8: declarations *)
declaration = [ "export" ] ( [ "bound" ] bindable | "shared" shareable | decl ) ;
bindable    = "global" NAME type | "array" NAME type capacity | "buffer" NAME capacity ;
shareable   = bindable | "list" NAME type capacity | "index" NAME NAME PATH ;
decl        = "const" NAME literal
            | "err" NAME
            | "list" NAME type capacity | "queue" NAME type capacity | "pool" NAME NAME capacity
            | "record" NAME { field | "big_endian" } "end"
            | "type" NAME ( "int" | "bool" | "str" | "dec" INT | "proc" effect "end" )
            | "index" NAME NAME PATH
            | "tasks" NAME capacity [ size [ size [ size ] ] ] [ "apart" ]
            | "extern" c-name effect "from" STRING [ "as" NAME ] "end"
            | "test" NAME "do" { body } "end" ;
capacity    = size | "host" ;
size        = INT | NAME ;
field       = NAME NAME [ size ] ;
c-name      = NAME | reserved-procedure | STRING ;
row-item    = [ "export" ] "row" NAME [ "as" NAME ] { value } "." ;
assign-item = "assign" NAME "(" value { "," value } ")" ;
value       = literal | NAME ;

(* 9: procedures *)
definition  = [ "export" ] "def" NAME effect "do" { body } "end" ;
effect      = [ params ] [ "gives" params ] [ "or" "fail" ] ;
params      = param { "," param } ;
param       = [ NAME ] ( type | coll-type | "args" ) ;          (* args: an input only, 16.13 *)
type        = [ "owned" ] ( NAME [ size ] ) ;      (* a proc type is declared by a type, 7.4 *)
coll-type   = ( "array" | "list" | "queue" ) NAME [ size ] | "buffer" ;   (* an input, 9.9 *)

(* 9 to 11: the body *)
body        = literal | NAME | PATH | store | set | fits | block | cat | args-value | guard | control | defer
            | "," | "."                                       (* the end of a statement, 10.8 *)
            | "return" | "fail" | ( "break" | "continue" ) [ INT ] "." ;
store       = "to" ( NAME | PATH ) ;   (* a local, or a field *)
set         = "set" ( NAME | PATH ) ;                         (* a global, 9.4 *)
fits        = "fits" ( NAME | PATH ) ;                        (* a str N place, 7.3 *)
block       = "do" { "to" NAME } { body } "end"
            | "def" effect "do" { body } "end"              (* a block value, 10.5 *)
            | "ref" NAME ;
cat         = "args" { body } "." "cat" | "cat" ;           (* 9.8; a bare cat takes an args parameter, 16.13 *)
args-value  = "args" { body } "." ;                           (* 16.13 *)
guard       = "or_fail" | "or_return" | "or_else" [ "to" NAME ] { body } "end" ;
control     = "if" { body } [ "else" { body } ] "end"
            | "loop" { body } "end"
            | "match" { branch } [ "otherwise" { body } "end" ] "end" ;
defer       = "defer" { body } "end" ;             (* 10.7 *)
branch      = "when" case-value { case-value } "do" { body } "end" ;
case-value  = literal | NAME | PATH ;

(3) A source read by data load follows data-source of 13.4.

Annex B Diagnostics (informative)§

(1) This annex collects the messages of the diagnostics tables of the clauses. They are the texts this implementation prints (4 (3)). The left column is the clause that lists the message.

(2) A refusal is printed as file:line:column: message. The line and column are those of the token at which the processor knew: something missing is known at the token after it, a value left over at the end of the definition. In a message, name, s, i and buf stand for places, not procedures, and the short code after a colon shows the right form.

ClauseMessage
6this character is not allowed outside literals and remarks
6a dot is followed by a name, with no space
6a number must not run into letters, an underscore or a dot
6a sign is attached to its number; arithmetic uses procedures (add, sub)
6the integer does not fit in 64 bits
6a decimal has at most 18 digits after the point
6the decimal does not fit in 64 bits at its scale
6an underscore stands between two digits
6the string is not closed on its line
6unknown escape; a raw string r"..." keeps backslashes as written
6the escape is not a code point
6the only prefix of a string is r (raw string)
6a character literal holds one character
6this source is written for another format version; this build reads version 2
7a bool is expected here
7this procedure takes two values of one type: u8 with u8, int with int; u8 and raw convert
7the constant is outside the range of this type; low_u8 and the others keep the low bits
7u8, u16, u32, u64, i8, i16, i32 and low_u8 ... are made from an int or from one another; for a declared type take raw first
7u_shr takes an int or an unsigned type; a signed type shifts with shr
7u_div, u_mod, floor_div and floor_mod take an int or an unsigned type
7u_lt, u_le, u_gt and u_ge take an int or an unsigned type; a signed type compares with lt
7rotl and rotr take an int or a u64; for a narrow type take raw
7mul_hi and u_mul_hi take an int or a u64; for a narrow type take raw

7a field holds str N; a str view lives only in locals, arguments and results
7two dec values of different scales: rescale one first (d 2 rescale)
7a dec is divided by an int, not by a dec; for a share, rescale first and divide by the int
7dec A times dec B is dec A+B, and A+B is at most 18; rescale one first
7dec N has 0 to 18 digits after the point

8this name is not declared before this place

Annex D Not in this edition (informative)§

(1) The following have a place in the design but are not accepted by the processor of this edition; using them is refused at load. This document does not define their meaning until a later edition does.

  • The rest of float (7.7): the module math of mathematical functions (square root, floor, exponential, logarithm, trigonometric functions), record fields f32 f64, types declared over float, match, and real arguments of extern.
  • Declarations defined by users (make, 6.6 (5)).
  • Records held inside records, and the field-by-field layout columns.
  • The compression module deflate.
  • Record fields of a declared type, of err or of a handle type; a field takes the widths of 8.8 only.
